analysis: New vs the 4am brief: the single biggest fresh item is Fed Chair Warsh's Bangkok speech tonight (11:30pm ET) — the last scheduled Fed word before Saturday's blackout, with October hike odds now a coin toss (Reuters, ~1h old). Futures are still split: Dow +0.23%, S&P -0.32%, Nasdaq 100 -1.2% — the growth-vs-value split from Wednesday is persisting rather than healing. Tesla has its own catalyst tonight (Roadster demo 5:55pm PT) plus a Barclays Tesla-SpaceX merger note, with TSLA -2% premarket. The chip trade added two single-source wrinkles: ByteDance-MediaTek custom AI chip talks (Nvidia-moat narrative) and a Taiwan push to settle Micron's HBM bonus dispute before a strike — treat both as fragile. Banks showed the tape's mood: BofA missed on a $1.2B regulatory charge and MS beat cleanly yet both fell Wednesday; macro is overwhelming stock-specific results right now. TSMC remains the bullish counter-signal — record Q3, 44% full-year revenue growth guide, 2nm at 8% of wafer revenue, 2026 capex held at $60-64B — yet TSM fell ~2% overnight anyway: the market is de-rating AI credit risk, not re-examining AI demand. Signal vs noise: CoreWeave's ~15% bond yields and the Gartner neocloud warning are real credit stress, but company-specific so far; watch PPI/retail sales/jobless claims at 5:30am PT today and Warsh tonight for the next repricing.

community_signals.takeaway: HN discussion is tracking CoreWeave's bond selloff (yields near 15%) and Musk's one-word 'Yikes' reaction, framing the episode as credit-market discipline on the debt-funded AI buildout rather than an equity valuation blip. Still the freshest HN thread on the day's dominant story; no newer qualifying threads found.

headlines.headline: Fed Chair Warsh speaks at the IMF meeting in Bangkok at 11:30pm ET tonight (8:30pm PT) — his last scheduled remarks before Saturday's blackout ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC. After hot September CPI, an October hike is now seen as a coin toss (CME <40% late Wednesday), and Fed colleagues are publicly pushing back on Warsh's 'quiet Fed' communications stance.
headlines.why_it_matters: Last word on rates before the decision — with odds near 50/50, every phrase moves hike expectations, and hike repricing is exactly what is squeezing AI-infrastructure credit.

headlines.headline: Tesla's Roadster demo goes live tonight 7:55pm CT (5:55pm PT) in Waco, TX — rescheduled from Oct 1 on high winds; Musk calls it a 'candidate for greatest product demo of all time.' Separately, a Barclays note floated a possible Tesla-SpaceX merger announcement before Tesla's early-December annual meeting, with an all-stock SpaceX acquisition of Tesla seen as the more likely structure.
headlines.why_it_matters: TSLA fell ~2% premarket on merger chatter plus broad tech weakness; the event is a pure sentiment catalyst ahead of TSLA earnings on Oct 21. Confirmed event and note — the merger itself is analyst speculation, not announced.

headlines.headline: Reuters Morning Bid leads with 'CoreWeave unravels': shares down another ~5.6% premarket after a 15% Wednesday slide on debt fears. The CEO reaffirmed confidence in the $99B backlog, ARK bought 189K shares Wednesday, and Dan Ives called the fears 'way overdone.'
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI-credit stress trade is deepening for a second day — CoreWeave's bond yields near 15% are the epicenter; the question is whether it stays company-specific or spreads to hyperscalers.

headlines.headline: Reports say ByteDance is in advanced talks with MediaTek on custom AI data center chips; separately, Taiwan's president urged Micron management and unions to settle bonus disputes to avoid a strike at Micron's Taiwan HBM packaging hub. NVDA -1.7%, MU -4.4% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Custom-silicon chatter pressures Nvidia's AI-moat narrative, and an HBM packaging disruption would hit the memory trade — single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile.

headlines.headline: Bank results recap (Wed): BofA missed on a $1.2B regulatory charge (AML failures; adjusted EPS $1.08 vs $1.10 est.), shares -5.9%. Morgan Stanley beat cleanly (EPS $3.03 vs ~$2.92 est., record $9.1B wealth revenue, $232B net new assets) but still fell ~3.5%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Even a clean beat got sold on the risk-off tape — on this tape, macro is overwhelming stock-specific results.

headlines.headline: Mixed premarket split persists: Dow futures +0.23% while S&P 500 futures -0.32% and Nasdaq 100 futures -1.2%; the Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS) is down 1%+ premarket as NVDA (-1.7%) and META (-1%) lag while AAPL (+<1%) holds up a day after its first $5T close.
headlines.why_it_matters: The growth-vs-value split from Wednesday is widening — the open is set to be tech-led again, with futures tilted negative.
